Command 1: node scripts/t01-next-identity-compatibility-smoke.mjs --bskel-root <bskel checkout at 7cabdb5ebeab70985d23d6f33b0990151e5958a9> --consumer-commit ebfff2205244f4866655476a828f05b9bf971cff --out <result file>. It exited 0, and the result file has summary total 12, passed 12, failed 0, not_run 0 and conformance_pack.byte_sha256 2df0d860428cb8b6bcc1bcdb560f06ccd1257b3937af65448011a1f0d0c1ec42, which is the sha256 of the file schemas/next/identity-conformance.json. The script runs npm pack on both repositories, installs both tarballs into one scratch project (so backend-skeleton is installed there), requires six schema and data files of the installed becoder package to be byte-identical to the installed backend-skeleton copies, and replays the pack through the installed becoder reader. Command 2: node --test test/next-identity-consumer-result.test.mjs test/next-identity-consumer.test.mjs test/t01-next-identity-compatibility-smoke.test.mjs printed tests 9, pass 9, fail 0, cancelled 0, skipped 0 (2 + 6 + 1 in the order given; the third file only matches the source text of the smoke script against patterns and does not run it). In the result, execution.exit_code, execution.bskel_runtime_imported and execution.bskel_runtime_spawned are constants written by the result builder (lib/next/identity-consumer-result.mjs lines 91 to 93) and execution.command is a fixed template of the smoke script (line 87); none of them is an observation of this run. What was read instead: the reader lib/next/identity-consumer.mjs imports only node:crypto and lib/contract-ref.mjs, which imports only node:crypto, and package.json lists only ajv and ajv-formats as dependencies.

consumer_set.step_2_set_check: BECODER_RESULT=<path of the becoder result file written by the first command> BEVAL_ROOT=<beval checkout at 3119c8f8711cdaee665e79345498d2210910fed1> node --input-type=module -e 'import fs from "node:fs"; import path from "node:path"; import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url"; const { verifyRequiredConsumerSet } = await import("./contracts/next/consumer-conformance.mjs"); const { replayIdentityConformanceBytes } = await import(pathToFileURL(path.join(process.env.BEVAL_ROOT, "lib/next-runtime/identity-consumer.mjs")).href); const pack = fs.readFileSync("schemas/next/identity-conformance.json"); const becoder = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.env.BECODER_RESULT, "utf8")); const beval = replayIdentityConformanceBytes(pack, { consumerCommit: "3119c8f8711cdaee665e79345498d2210910fed1" }); console.log(JSON.stringify(verifyRequiredConsumerSet(pack, [becoder, beval], { required_repositories: ["popixoxipop-collab/backend-decoder", "popixoxipop-collab/Backend-evaluation"] })));'
consumer_set.step_2_how_to_run: Run it with the working directory set to a backend-skeleton checkout at 7cabdb5ebeab70985d23d6f33b0990151e5958a9. Replace <path of the becoder result file written by the first command> with the path used in step 1 and <beval checkout at 3119c8f8711cdaee665e79345498d2210910fed1> with the path of a Backend-evaluation checkout at that commit. It prints the consumer set as one line of JSON.
consumer_set.beval_result: Not a file: the command calls replayIdentityConformanceBytes from lib/next-runtime/identity-consumer.mjs of the beval checkout (not from an installed tarball) with consumerCommit 3119c8f8711cdaee665e79345498d2210910fed1, so the beval result carries the commit given there and the default execution.command of that function.
consumer_set.binding_limits: verifyRequiredConsumerSet checks each consumer commit_sha only as 40 lowercase hex characters (COMMIT_RE, contracts/next/consumer-conformance.mjs line 7, used at lines 74 and 112). It does not tie the commit to the bytes that were replayed. Reproduced on 2026-10-02 with the command in step_2_set_check plus one assignment inserted before the console.log call (for example becoder.consumer.commit_sha = "0".repeat(40);): a becoder result whose consumer.commit_sha was replaced by forty zeros was still ACCEPTED and the set carried the forty zeros; a beval result whose commit_sha was replaced by forty f was still ACCEPTED; a becoder result whose execution.command was replaced by 'echo not-a-run' was still ACCEPTED. Still REJECTED: a changed cases[0].observed, summary.passed set to 11, execution.exit_code 1, execution.bskel_runtime_imported true, a zeroed conformance_pack.byte_sha256, and a set with only one of the two required repositories.

current_rerun.limits: The consumer commit inside each result is a claim made by the run, not an observation of it: becoder takes it from --consumer-commit or, when that is absent, from git rev-parse HEAD (scripts/t01-next-identity-compatibility-smoke.mjs line 86); beval takes it from git rev-parse HEAD (scripts/package-install-smoke.mjs line 50); neither script checks that the working tree is clean, and the verifier checks only that the commit is 40 hex characters (see consumer_set.binding_limits). For this block the backend-decoder and Backend-evaluation checkouts were at the heads above and git status --porcelain printed nothing when checked after the runs, and the bskel tree was exported from that exact commit with git archive (every file equal to the commit's tree; only a node_modules link was added), so the commits are right for these runs, but nothing in a result proves it. execution.exit_code, execution.bskel_runtime_imported and execution.bskel_runtime_spawned are constants written by the result builders, not observations. GitHub Actions runs on these heads were not read for this block. No rollback material for T01-06 was found (see test/contract-next/t01-compatibility-evidence.json current_state.not_established). Nothing here shows a release, a default-writer change, a cutover, or runtime behaviour of any consumer beyond the 12 reviewed identity vectors.
